sol-cfc/n4-38-en-garden-path analysis 0.sentence: The old man the boats while the young sleep.

derivationStages.statement: Build the three nominal expressions, treating “the old” and “the young” as plural human nominals.
derivationStages.stageRecord: In this sentence, “the old” denotes old people and “the young” denotes young people. Each is represented as a DP containing an adjectival modifier and a silent plural human nominal head. This establishes the human interpretation and plural features of the two expressions without positing an antecedent for noun ellipsis. “The boats” is an ordinary DP with an overt plural noun. The subsequent predicate structure will identify “man” as a verb, rather than as the noun initially suggested by the opening words.

values.nominalHeadStatus: silent human nominal, not antecedent-dependent ellipsis
silent human nominal, not antecedent-dependent ellipsis

derivationStages.statement: Construct the two predicates and establish their thematic and object-Case relations.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The verb “man,” meaning staff or operate, takes “the boats” as its DP complement and assigns it the Theme role. It governs this complement and assigns accusative Case. “The old” is introduced in the main VP's specifier as the Agent of manning. The intransitive verb “sleep” forms a separate VP with “the young” in its specifier, receiving the external Sleeper role. Neither subject has yet moved to a finite subject position. Separate silent present-tense I heads are introduced for the two clauses; their plural agreement will be established when the subjects occupy Spec-IP.

derivationStages.statement: Form the finite clause “the young sleep” by subject A-movement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The subordinate I head takes the sleep VP as its complement. “The young” moves from the previously established Spec-VP to Spec-IP, leaving an unpronounced DP trace. This A-movement satisfies the finite clause's subject requirement without assigning a second theta-role. Finite I licenses nominative Case on the raised DP and agrees with its plural features. Its present-tense dependency is realized by the unmarked plural form “sleep,” which remains in V rather than undergoing overt V-to-I movement. The raised DP c-commands and locally A-binds its VP-internal trace within this IP, satisfying the local binding requirement on the NP-trace.

values.motivation: finite subject requirement and nominative licensing
values.thetaRolePreservation: one Sleeper role for the A-chain

values.configuration: the subject c-commands its coindexed VP-internal trace

derivationStages.statement: Attach the finite temporal clause headed by “while” to the main VP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Temporal “while” is analyzed as C and selects the completed finite IP “the young sleep.” The resulting CP is right-adjoined to the main VP, rather than selected as an argument of “man.” This preserves the verb's existing argument structure and establishes a temporal-overlap relation between the manning of the boats and the young people's sleeping. The main subject remains in its original Spec-VP position at this stage.

values.interpretation: the manning and sleeping situations overlap in time

derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix clause: “The old man the boats while the young sleep.”
derivationStages.stageRecord: The matrix I head takes the temporally modified VP as its complement. “The old” moves from its established VP-internal position to matrix Spec-IP, leaving a silent DP trace and satisfying the finite subject requirement while preserving its Agent theta-role. Matrix finite I licenses nominative Case and agrees with this plural human subject. Present tense is realized by the unmarked plural verb form “man,” which remains in V. The raised subject locally A-binds its trace within the matrix IP. A silent declarative C closes the root clause. The resulting pronounced sequence is exactly the input: “old” belongs to the subject nominal, “man” is the transitive matrix verb, and the while-clause supplies the temporal adjunct.

values.motivation: finite subject requirement and nominative licensing
values.thetaRolePreservation: one Agent role for the A-chain

values.configuration: the subject c-commands its coindexed VP-internal trace

opus-final/n4-13-fr-long-relative analys.sentence: Le livre que Marie pensait que Jean avait déjà lu se trouvait encore sur la table de la cuisine.

derivationStages.statement: The participle lu merges with a silent relative operator, forming the most deeply embedded VP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Derivation starts in the lowest clause. The participle lu takes its object first. That object is not the overt noun livre but a silent relative operator, which will later raise to the edge of the relative clause. Theta-assignment gives the operator the Theme role of lu, so the gap after lu is an argument position and not an adjunct gap.

derivationStages.statement: Transitive v* merges, the participle raises to it, and Jean is merged as the external argument.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent transitive v* merges with the VP headed by lu. The participle then head-moves and adjoins to v*, leaving an unpronounced trace inside VP. This movement relation links the raised participle, its trace and the v* host. Jean is then externally merged as the specifier of the resulting v*P. Theta-assignment gives Jean the Agent role of reading.

derivationStages.statement: The operator moves to the edge of the lowest v*P phase, the participle agrees with it, and déjà adjoins.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The v*P headed by lu is a phase. The relative operator must leave it, so it first raises to an outer specifier of v*P, leaving a trace in object position. This internal merge connects the raised operator, its trace and the v*P it merges with. From this edge position the operator is a preceding object for the participle. Participle agreement therefore holds between lu and the operator, inheriting the masculine singular features of livre; the form lu shows no overt ending. Finally the adverb déjà is pair-merged to v*P as an adjunct. It sits above the operator's landing site so that it precedes lu.

derivationStages.statement: Finite T, spelled out as the auxiliary avait, agrees with Jean, and Jean raises to Spec-TP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The finite pluperfect auxiliary avait merges as the T head of the embedded clause, taking the v*P as its complement. T probes downward and Agree holds with Jean in Spec-v*P. This values third-person singular agreement on avait and nominative Case on Jean. Jean then raises to Spec-TP, leaving a trace in its theta position. This internal merge links Jean, its trace and the T projection, and puts Jean before avait déjà lu.

derivationStages.statement: The declarative complementizer que closes the embedded clause, and the operator moves to its edge.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The second que, which introduces the complement of pensait, merges as a declarative C over the embedded TP. CP is a phase, so the relative operator continues its successive-cyclic movement. It raises from the v*P edge to Spec-CP, leaving another trace. This internal merge links the operator, the trace at the v*P edge and the C projection. From Spec-CP the operator is accessible to the higher clause.

derivationStages.statement: The verb pensait takes the embedded CP as its complement.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The attitude verb pensait merges with the embedded clause que Jean avait déjà lu. Theta-assignment makes that CP the propositional complement of pensait. The operator remains at the edge of that complement.

derivationStages.statement: v* merges over the pensait VP, the verb raises to v*, and Marie is merged as the external argument.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent v* merges with the VP headed by pensait. The finite verb head-moves to v*, leaving a trace before its CP complement. This movement relation links the raised verb, its trace and the v* host. Marie is then externally merged in Spec-v*P. Theta-assignment gives Marie the Experiencer role of thinking.

derivationStages.statement: The operator moves to the edge of the higher v*P phase.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The v*P headed by pensait is a phase. The operator would become inaccessible once its complement is transferred, so it moves from the edge of the embedded CP to an outer specifier of this v*P. This internal merge links the operator, the trace it leaves in the lower Spec-CP and the higher v*P.

derivationStages.statement: Silent past T agrees with Marie, the verb complex raises to T, and Marie raises to Spec-TP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent finite past T merges with the higher v*P. T first probes and Agree holds with Marie, valuing third-person singular, spelled out on pensait, and nominative Case. French finite lexical verbs raise to T, so the v* complex containing pensait head-moves and adjoins to T, leaving a trace in v*. This movement relation links that complex, its trace and the T host. Marie then raises to Spec-TP, leaving a trace in Spec-v*P. This internal merge links Marie, its trace and the T projection. The result is the order Marie pensait.

derivationStages.statement: The relative complementizer que merges, and the operator reaches its final landing site in the relative Spec-CP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The first que of the sentence merges as a relative C over the clause Marie pensait que Jean avait déjà lu. Its relative feature attracts the operator, which raises from the higher v*P edge to Spec-CP. This internal merge links the operator, its last trace and the relative C projection. It completes the long-distance dependency that began in the object position of lu.

derivationStages.statement: The relative clause adjoins to the noun livre, the operator is bound by livre, and the determiner le completes the subject DP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The noun livre is introduced, and the completed relative CP is pair-merged to it as a restrictive adjunct. Through relative binding, livre identifies the operator in Spec-CP, so the clause is interpreted as a predicate of books. This also supplies the masculine singular features that the participle agreement depends on. The determiner le then merges with this nominal, completing the DP le livre que Marie pensait que Jean avait déjà lu.

derivationStages.statement: The prepositional phrase de la cuisine is built as a separate object.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Next to the finished subject DP, the workspace builds la cuisine and merges it with the preposition de. Case assignment gives that DP oblique Case from de. The resulting PP waits as an independent object until it can modify table.

derivationStages.statement: The PP de la cuisine adjoins to table, and the locative PP sur la table de la cuisine is completed.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The noun table is introduced, and de la cuisine is pair-merged to it as a modifier, giving the kitchen table reading. The determiner la then merges, and the preposition sur takes the resulting DP. Case assignment gives that DP oblique Case from sur. The locative PP and the subject DP remain separate roots.

derivationStages.statement: The verb trouvait merges with the locative PP, and the complex subject DP is merged as its internal argument.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Locative se trouver has no agent. Its subject is an internal argument, so trouvait first merges with the PP sur la table de la cuisine, which theta-assignment makes its Location. The full DP headed by livre is then merged into Spec-VP. Theta-assignment gives it the Theme role of being located. This unites the two separate roots.

derivationStages.statement: Non-agentive v, spelled out as the clitic se, merges, trouvait raises to it, and encore adjoins to vP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A non-agentive v head, spelled out as the inherent reflexive clitic se, merges with the VP. Voice marking records that se signals the absence of an external argument for trouvait, so no agent is introduced. The verb trouvait then head-moves to this v, leaving a trace before the PP. In the resulting complex the proclitic se is linearized before the verb. This movement relation links trouvait, its trace and the se host. Finally the adverb encore is pair-merged to vP. Because the verb will later raise past it, encore will follow se trouvait.

derivationStages.statement: Matrix T agrees with the subject DP, se trouvait raises to T, and the subject DP raises to Spec-TP.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent finite past T merges with the vP. T probes and Agree holds with the internal-argument DP headed by livre, valuing third-person singular, spelled out on trouvait, and nominative Case. The complex se trouvait head-moves and adjoins to T, crossing encore and leaving a trace in v. This movement relation links that complex, its trace and the T host. The whole subject DP, relative clause included, then raises to Spec-TP, leaving a trace in Spec-VP. This internal merge links the subject DP, its trace and the T projection. The order is now subject, se trouvait, encore, PP.

derivationStages.statement: A silent declarative C completes the matrix clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: The root clause is a declarative assertion with no overt complementizer, so a silent C merges over the matrix TP. Clause typing marks the whole clause as declarative. This yields the complete sentence.

opus-final/n4-07-en-cleft-relative analy.sentence: It was the manager who insisted that the report which the interns had prepared be rewritten before Friday.

derivationStages.statement: The relative-clause verb 'prepared' merges with the relative operator 'which' as its object.
derivationStages.stageRecord: As in the other reading, the relative pronoun 'which' is first merged as the object of 'prepared', the source of the object gap in the relative clause. Theta-assignment: 'prepared' assigns the Theme role to 'which'.

derivationStages.statement: A silent transitive v merges, values accusative on 'which', and introduces 'the interns' as Agent.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent transitive light verb merges with the verb phrase headed by 'prepared'. Agree: it values accusative Case on 'which'. Separately, 'the interns' is assembled and then merged as the specifier of the light verb. Theta-assignment: the light verb assigns the Agent role to 'the interns'.

derivationStages.statement: Perfect 'had' merges as T, agrees with 'the interns', and the subject raises to its specifier.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Perfect 'had' merges as the tense head of the relative clause. Agree: 'had' values its phi-features and nominative Case on 'the interns'. Internal merge: the subject then raises to the specifier of 'had' for EPP, leaving a silent trace in the Agent position.

derivationStages.statement: A silent relative C merges and attracts 'which' to its edge.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent relative complementizer merges with the clause headed by 'had'. Agree: it matches the relative/wh features of 'which'. Internal merge: 'which' then moves to its specifier, leaving a silent trace in object position.

derivationStages.statement: The relative clause adjoins to 'report', and 'the' completes the report nominal.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 'report' is introduced and the relative clause is pair-merged to it. Adjunction: the relative clause becomes a restrictive adjunct of 'report'. Operator-binding: 'which' is identified with 'report'. Then 'the' merges with the modified noun phrase.

derivationStages.statement: Passive 'rewritten' takes the report nominal as Theme, with no temporal modifier at this level.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 'rewritten' merges with the report nominal. Theta-assignment: 'rewritten' assigns the Theme role to that nominal. Unlike the low-attachment reading, 'before Friday' is not merged inside the embedded clause, because here it will date the insisting rather than the rewriting.

derivationStages.statement: Passive auxiliary 'be' merges with the bare participial predicate.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Bare passive 'be' merges with the participle phrase headed by 'rewritten'. Selection: 'be' selects a passive participle, so no Agent of rewriting is projected.

derivationStages.statement: Silent subjunctive T merges, agrees with the report nominal, and raises it to subject position.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent subjunctive tense head merges above 'be'. Agree: it values nominative Case on the report nominal, with no overt agreement on 'be'. Internal merge: the report nominal then raises to its specifier for EPP, leaving a silent trace after 'rewritten'.

derivationStages.statement: The complementizer 'that' merges with the subjunctive clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 'that' merges with the subjunctive clause. Clause-typing: 'that' types it as a finite subjunctive declarative complement.

derivationStages.statement: 'insisted' takes the that-clause, and 'before Friday' adjoins high to the insisting predicate.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 'insisted' merges with the that-clause. Theta-assignment: 'insisted' assigns the clause its propositional role. Mood-selection: as a mandative verb, 'insisted' licenses the subjunctive. Next, 'before' merges with 'Friday', and case-assignment gives 'Friday' oblique Case. Adjunction: the temporal phrase is pair-merged to the predicate headed by 'insisted'. In this reading the insisting, not the rewriting, took place before Friday; the string is unchanged because the adjunct still follows the that-clause.

values.type: temporal modifier of the insisting event

derivationStages.statement: A silent v merges and 'who' is merged as the Agent of insisting.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent light verb merges with the modified insisting predicate, and 'who' is externally merged in its specifier. Theta-assignment: the light verb assigns the Agent role to 'who'.

derivationStages.statement: Silent past T merges, agrees with 'who' and 'insisted', and raises 'who' to subject position.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent past-tense head merges. Agree: it values nominative Case and agreement with 'who'. Tense-agreement: past tense is valued on 'insisted'. Internal merge: 'who' then raises to the specifier of the tense head for EPP, leaving a silent trace.

derivationStages.statement: A silent relative C merges and attracts 'who' to its edge, forming the cleft clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent relative complementizer merges. Agree: it matches the relative/wh features of 'who'. Internal merge: 'who' then moves from subject position to its specifier, leaving a silent trace.

derivationStages.statement: The pivot 'the manager' is built and the cleft clause adjoins to it.
derivationStages.stageRecord: 'the manager' is assembled and the cleft clause is pair-merged to it. Adjunction: the cleft clause becomes an adjunct of the pivot. Operator-binding: 'who' is identified with 'the manager'.

derivationStages.statement: Copular 'was' merges, and expletive 'It' fills its specifier, yielding the it-cleft.
derivationStages.stageRecord: Copular 'was' merges with the pivot and its cleft clause. EPP-satisfaction: the expletive 'It' is merged as the specifier of 'was'. Agree: 'was' agrees with 'It' and assigns it nominative Case. Cleft-focus: 'the manager' is the exhaustively identified focus, the cleft clause is the background, and 'It' is linked to that clause.

derivationStages.statement: A silent declarative C completes the matrix clause.
derivationStages.stageRecord: A silent declarative complementizer merges with the matrix clause. Clause-typing: it types the sentence as a declarative assertion, which completes the derivation.
